title: State (behavioral)
points: Each state of an object is its own class implementing a shared state interface: same methods, different logic and allowed transitions.
The object delegates to its current state and swaps it on a transition. A state machine without a giant if/else on a status field.
trade: Makes invalid transitions explicit and new states a new class (OCP). One class per state, so for 2-3 simple states an enum and switch is simpler (KISS). Unlike strategies, states know about each other because they return the next state.
test: Why is State better than an if (status == ...) chain once an order has 6 statuses? How does it differ from Strategy?
answer: Each state owns its own rules and transitions, so there is no sprawling conditional and adding a state is a new class. Strategy is picked from outside and doesn't switch itself; State objects trigger the next state.

questions.question: An Order moves Created, Paid, Shipped, Cancelled, and each status allows different actions. Which pattern models this best?
questions.explanation: State: each status is a class with the same methods but different logic and transitions, so no status if/else chain.
